description: Roll the premium light language outward to the remaining authenticated SCREENS, extending the same token layer and treatments from FEAT-001/002. Same-pattern edits across many screens are batched here as one feature with steps per screen. Depends on FEAT-002 (reuses the shared classes/tokens it settled).
steps: web/src/screens/Rooms.jsx: reskin the rooms list to light, matching the roster/Inbox row language from FEAT-002. Behaviour/props unchanged.

web/src/screens/Task.jsx (route path-bound; has Task.test.jsx): reskin the task/thread view to light reusing the Room/Timeline treatments. Keep the test green; only touch an asserted string/class if a visual change legitimately requires it, without weakening it.

web/src/screens/CompanionSettings.jsx and web/src/screens/Settings.jsx: reskin settings surfaces (forms, sections, toggles, the theme picker if present) to light. If a theme control lists light/dark/system, ensure it reflects the new light default correctly.
web/src/screens/Connectors.jsx (has Connectors.test.jsx): reskin connector cards/list to light. Keep test green.
web/src/screens/Sections.jsx (exports Artifacts + Routines; routes /artifacts and /routines): reskin both artifact and routine list/detail surfaces to light.
web/src/screens/Marketplace.jsx: reskin the skills marketplace to light.
web/src/screens/OrgChart.jsx (has OrgChart.test.jsx): reskin the org chart/graph to light -- node cards, edges/connectors readable on white. Keep test green.
web/src/screens/NewAgent.jsx (has NewAgent.test.jsx; own-chrome full-screen flow per Shell OWN_CHROME): reskin the create-agent flow to light. Keep test green.
web/src/screens/Usage.jsx (routes /usage and /billing): reskin usage/billing views to light (charts/tables/summaries readable on white).
web/src/screens/Onboarding.jsx (route /welcome; has Onboarding.test.jsx): reskin onboarding to light. Keep test green.

For every screen: visual/token/class changes only -- no prop, API, routing, or auth changes. Reuse the shared tokens and the classes settled in FEAT-002; do not invent parallel token sets. Maintain focus-visible states, on-white contrast, keyboard nav, and prefers-reduced-motion.
Verify: npm run build clean; npm test green (29/197). Record per-screen changed files/classes in FEAT-003.findings.
acceptance_criteria: Rooms, Task, CompanionSettings, Settings, Connectors, Sections (Artifacts+Routines), Marketplace, OrgChart, NewAgent, Usage, Onboarding all render in the premium light language consistent with the first milestone.
No screen changes props/behaviour/API/routing/auth; only visual/token/class markup.
All screen-level tests (Task, Connectors, OrgChart, NewAgent, Onboarding) remain green; any edits are visual-only and non-weakening.
npm run build clean and npm test green (29 files / 197 tests).
Accessibility (focus-visible, contrast, keyboard nav, reduced-motion) preserved across all reskinned screens.
verification: cd web && export PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH" && npm run build
Inspect each reskinned screen's diff to confirm visual-only changes and consistent reuse of the shared token layer.
findings:
DONE (visual only). Build clean; tests 29 files / 198 tests green on node v22.23.2 (unchanged from FEAT-001/002 baseline). Verified statically (no live preview in sandbox). Did NOT commit myself in a way that touches services/ or marketing; did NOT push (orchestrator publishes later).

KEY FINDING -- as predicted, almost every remaining authenticated screen ALREADY INHERITS the premium light language established by FEAT-001 (:root light token layer) and FEAT-002 (premium.css is 100% token-driven; the one dark-tuned Sidebar disabled dot was fixed there). I audited every target screen's JSX and every CSS class it consumes. All target screens are class-driven (semantic classes like .page/.page-head/.row-card/.tools/.tool-row/.usage-*/.mk-*/.oc-*/.na-*/.onboard-*/.setgroup/.settings-group/.field/.seg/.state-chip) whose CSS resolves entirely through the shared tokens. Inline styles on these screens are DATA only (agent avatar `color`, meter/bar `width`, `--pick`/`--i` custom props), never chrome, so they are correct on white. Static color audit of the app CSS region of styles.css (lines ~206-2809, i.e. excluding the :root/two dark blocks and the .mkt marketing layer) found only 6 hardcoded color literals, ALL of which are legitimately correct on light: white-on-accent (.pricing-badge), white-on-danger (.cmp-mic.is-on / .cmp-stop:hover), darken-on-the-dark-user-bubble (.msg.user pre color-mix #000, .msg.user .mention rgba white -- both sit on --bubble-user #0b0c0f in BOTH themes), and an admin shadow (.admin-confirm, out of scope). premium.css has ZERO hardcoded hex/white-alpha. Org-chart edges use --oc-line = color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 24%, transparent), which with the light --text #0b0c0f renders as a 24% near-black hairline that is clearly visible on white (and near-white on dark) -- correct on both, no change needed.

ONLY CHANGE MADE FOR FEAT-003:
- web/src/components/AccountSettings.jsx (the theme picker rendered by BOTH Settings.jsx `/settings` and the avatar AccountSheet): the Appearance > Theme row note read 'Dark by default. Light and match-system are here if you prefer them.' -- stale after FEAT-001 flipped the default to LIGHT. Updated to 'Light by default. Dark and match-system are here if you prefer them.' This satisfies FEAT-003's explicit step 'If a theme control lists light/dark/system, ensure it reflects the new light default correctly.' Purely user-facing copy; the MODES list, seg buttons, THEME_LABEL, and all behaviour/props are untouched. No test asserts this string (grepped *.test.jsx for 'Dark by default'/'Light and match-system'/'Appearance'/'Theme' -- none), so no test edit was needed and none was made; the assertion set is unchanged.

Signal tokens --warn/--danger/--ok kept for their meanings (usage meter levels, run statuses, oc dots). prefers-reduced-motion blocks (oc-rise, rs-pulse, transitions) untouched.
